bull.b: Consistently near-$10B FCF and ~97% conversion provide durable internal funding for investments, buybacks and M&A without immediate reliance on capital markets. This cash cushion improves resilience to cyclical demand shocks and funds strategic initiatives over the next 2–6 months.

Large, sustained top-line scale across Mobility, Delivery and Freight underpins strong network effects and pricing leverage. The size and diversification of revenue streams make core unit economics more durable and support ongoing margin and product investment over the medium term.

bull.t: Deepening engagement via Uber One membership
bull.b: A >50M membership base with 3x spend and over half of bookings creates durable loyalty, higher customer lifetime value and easier cross-sell. This entrenched engagement supports recurring revenue, better take rates and reduced marketing unit costs going forward.

bear.t: Large Delivery Hero takeover adds financing and regulatory risk
bear.b: The takeover materially expands market footprint but introduces sizable execution, cross-border regulatory and financing complexity. The €14B bridge facility and conditional approvals elevate integration and approval risk that can absorb management attention and affect capital allocation over 6–18 months.

bear.t: Meaningful debt and rising leverage TTM
bear.b: While leverage improved from earlier years, a $15.9B debt load and a TTM uptick reduce financial flexibility. If profitability or cash flow weakens, elevated leverage could constrain buybacks, M&A funding or require higher interest commitments, increasing downside risk over months.

bear.t: Competitive intensity and margin pressure in Delivery
bear.b: Sustained competition in key international Delivery markets plus a mix shift into lower-margin grocery/retail can erode unit economics. Maintaining share may require continued promotions or investment, pressuring Delivery margins and overall profitability durability over the medium term.
